solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hide outside pub stifling a tense laugh

indicators.note: something placed outside another wraps around it, so the hiding word goes round what follows
to stifle is to smother, so the outer word smothers the further letters by enclosing them too

blocks.note: a cache is a hidden store, a hiding place
an inn is a pub
taken as written
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone hides outside a pub, trying to muffle a nervous laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: The hiding place goes round both the pub and the A plus T that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cachinnate is to laugh loudly and immoderately, a rare literary verb.

clue.text: Firm doctor engaged in battle

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
to be at something, as in at work or at war, is to be engaged in it

explanation.surface: A company doctor is caught up in some fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged in' looks like a containment instruction, but it simply supplies a short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is armed fighting, the same as a battle between forces.

clue.text: A knight interrupts shrewd old king

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so these letters go inside the next word

blocks.note: cute can mean clever or shrewd
taken as written
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight barges in on a canny old monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Canute was the eleventh-century king of England, Denmark and Norway, famous for the tale of commanding the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: Canute is a historical monarch, so an example of an old king.

clue.text: There are no words to express such music!

definitions.text: There are no words to express such music!

blocks.clueFragment: There are no words to express such music!
blocks.note: surface reading: music so moving it leaves the listener speechless
setter's reading: literally, music that has no lyrics, played only on instruments

explanation.surface: Someone gushes that a piece of music is beyond description.
explanation.walkthrough: The stock phrase of rapture is read literally: music without any words in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrumental is a piece played without vocals, so it literally contains no words.

clue.text: Anorak – mostly green, found on road

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: green means new or inexperienced
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A green anorak is lying in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang an anorak is an obsessive enthusiast, named after the coats trainspotters wear, so it is not a garment here.
explanation.definitionFit: Anorak is British slang for a socially awkward obsessive, which is what a nerd is.

clue.text: Dine out and get desperately lost for words

indicators.note: acting desperately means acting wildly and without order, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone goes out to dinner and ends up hopelessly lost, and speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is both part of the letters and part of the surface's 'get lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tongue-tied means being unable to speak through shyness, the same as lost for words.

clue.text: Chieftain found back in Grimethorpe

indicators.note: found in says the letters are discovered sitting inside the next word
back means the letters are read going backwards

blocks.note: these letters sit inside the place name

explanation.surface: A tribal chief turns up back home in Grimethorpe.
explanation.walkthrough: Grimethorpe is a former mining village in South Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or commander, a chieftain in Arab lands.

clue.text: Decaying bone found in knoll

indicators.note: something found in a place is located within it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: a knoll is a small hill or mound
a rib is a bone

explanation.surface: A rotting bone is discovered in a small hillock.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund means near death or in terminal decline, so decaying.

clue.text: Left work to see Oliver, say, but with The Omen thrown in

indicators.note: something thrown in is tossed into the middle of something else

blocks.note: Oliver Reed was an English film actor; 'say' marks him as an example
an omen is a sign

explanation.surface: Someone quit their job to watch the film Oliver!, but got The Omen as a double bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver! and The Omen are both films, but here Oliver is a first name and The Omen is just an omen.
explanation.definitionFit: Resigned is the past tense of resign, to quit a job, so it means left work.

clue.text: In store men cooked soup

indicators.note: cooked food has been transformed from its raw state, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Staff in a shop have made some soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup.

clue.text: Needle returned with small knife

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to needle someone is to irk or annoy them
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A needle and a small knife have been handed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle' looks like a noun beside the knife, but it is the verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: Be about to eat fish up in club's spread

indicators.note: one word going about another and eating it encloses it
in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom upwards
in places the reversed letters inside the next word

blocks.note: a putter is a golf club
taken as written
tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: A golf club's buffet: be ready to eat fish there.
explanation.walkthrough: BE wraps round the fish, the whole is turned upside down, and it goes inside the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanut butter is a paste of ground nuts eaten spread on bread.

clue.text: Part of coaster nearly at the back

indicators.note: part of says the letters are only a section of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A section of a coastal vessel is close to the stern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' looks like a deletion signal, but its first letter is part of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word meaning behind or towards the rear of a ship.

clue.text: Imposing university start to grow dangerous organism

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: superb can mean magnificent or imposing
U is the abbreviation for university
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A grand university has begun growing a deadly microbe in its labs.
explanation.definitionFit: A superbug is a bacterium resistant to antibiotics, a dangerous organism.

clue.text: Damage trap erected beneath tree to get furry critter

indicators.note: erected means stood upright, which in a down clue turns the word to read bottom to top

blocks.note: a pine is a tree
to mar is to damage
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: Someone sets a trap under a tree to catch a furry animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beneath' places the damage and trap after the tree, since down clues read top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The pine marten is a small furry mammal of the weasel family living in woodland.

clue.text: Running pipe to dodgy canteen

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: a main is a principal water or gas pipe
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pipe is running to a shady works canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like part of the plumbing picture, but it is the definition, as in the running of a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The running or upkeep of a building or machine is its maintenance, keeping it in working order.

clue.text: Raced over bed when on enriched heart drug

indicators.note: turned over means upended, so the word reads the other way
the heart of a word is its central part, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: ran is the past tense of run, to race
a cot is a small bed
the two central letters of the eight-letter word

explanation.surface: A heart patient raced to bed when on an enriched drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the bed after the reversed racing word in this down clue, then the heart follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses, such as an opiate.

clue.text: Before batting supporter put suitable protection on cranium

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
a batsman who is batting is in
a box is the protective cup worn by a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: Before going in to bat, a player straps on proper head protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture suggests a helmet, but the protection is the groin guard called a box; 'before' and 'put on' just order the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainbox is a colloquial word for the skull, the box holding the brain.

clue.text: Understanding an order

blocks.note: first meaning: an agreement reached between parties
second meaning: a particular layout or sequence of things

explanation.walkthrough: Both meanings are nouns: a deal people come to, and the way items are set out.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement can be an informal agreement between people or the ordered placing of objects.

clue.text: Get sharp pain carrying artist's knife

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it within, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist hurts himself carrying a palette knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A parang is a heavy Malay knife used like a machete.

clue.text: Cardinal holds rare flower

indicators.note: a word that holds something keeps it inside

blocks.note: seven is a cardinal number
R is an abbreviation for rare

explanation.surface: A churchman is clutching an unusual bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is a counting number; 'flower' is something that flows, a river, the Severn running through Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is a river, a thing that flows, and the Severn is Britain's longest river.

clue.text: Delivery from pal on island

blocks.note: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate, a pal
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A parcel arrives from a friend living on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a chinaman is a left-arm bowler's wrist-spin delivery; 'on' places the island after the pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinaman is a specific kind of ball bowled in cricket, so a delivery in that sport's jargon.

clue.text: Doctor finally has a remedy without poison

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, its closing letter
without in its old sense means outside, so one word surrounds the others

blocks.note: a cure is a remedy
the closing letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: The doctor at last has a cure that contains no poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a plant extract used by South American peoples as an arrow poison.

clue.text: West Indian politician is a feeble person

blocks.note: WI is the abbreviation for West Indian or West Indies
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Caribbean politician is dismissed as a weakling.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a weak, timid person, someone feeble.

clue.text: TV channel

blocks.note: first meaning: informal word for television
second meaning: a pipe or duct carrying something

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one television station, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The tube is slang for the television set, and a tube is also a conduit through which things pass.

clue.text: Taking off for a show?

blocks.note: surface reading: an aircraft departing, or mimicking someone
setter's reading: removing clothes as a stage entertainment

explanation.surface: Someone is setting off, or doing an impression, to put on a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' wants to mean departing or impersonating; it is undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: This act is a performance in which the performer slowly undresses in front of an audience.

clue.text: Bone with neat calcium on the outside

indicators.note: something on the outside surrounds what it is placed with

blocks.note: Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: A bone comes neatly coated in calcium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like an adjective, but it is the archaic noun for a bovine.
explanation.definitionFit: The coxa is the hip bone, or the hip joint, in anatomy.

clue.text: Doddery grandpa gets lad round for a plant

indicators.note: doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the letters totter into a new order
going round something encloses it

blocks.note: a son is a lad
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shaky old grandfather gets a boy to come over and fetch a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden plant with flowers that open like a mouth.
